key_insight: In the FAIR-ICI cohort, survival extended beyond active immunotherapy for some patients, while real-world outcomes were often less favorable than pivotal trial results.
clinical_relevance: Performance status was important when interpreting outcomes: ECOG ≥2 was associated with poorer overall survival than ECOG 0–1.
method: Retrospective study of 3,231 adults receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors at four Belgian hospitals.
Harmonized electronic health records using OMOP-CDM and natural language processing.
Evaluated survival and treatment trajectories, with descriptive trial comparisons and multivariable Cox regression.
evidence_signal: Among 568 metastatic patients who discontinued immunotherapy without subsequent systemic therapy, median post-discontinuation survival was 21.4 months (95% CI 16.5–37.2), with 49.1% alive at 24 months.
watch_item: This observational treatment-outcomes study—not an AI drug-discovery study—cannot establish that discontinuation causes prolonged survival or that trial–practice differences reflect treatment effectiveness alone.
paper_title: Comprehensive real-world utilization, treatment trajectories, and outcomes of immune checkpoint inhibitors across cancer types: the multicenter FAIR-ICI cohort
